sections.title: Loss Estimates
sections.text:
The Loss Estimates presented here are believed to be reasonable, based on industry
experience, events postulated, and information provided by the client. The calculation of Loss
Expectancies is based on the review of building construction, operations, fire protection
systems, and fire protection features at the time of our assessment.  The estimates are further
based on conditions observed at the time of the visit.  By their nature, these estimates contain
some element of subjectivity.  Accordingly, the estimates cannot be taken as absolutes and
could be exceeded due to changes in physical conditions on site, or the initiating event or
escalation being more severe than anticipated within the boundaries of the estimate.
All damage and loss potential figures presented pertain exclusively to primary property
damage, associated contents damage, and associated business interruption recovery time
loss, caused directly by (fire or explosion) as defined in our Loss Estimate.

Loss Estimates Definitions:
Level
Definition
Level I
Primary Protection Systems are functioning and manual firefighting available
A loss event in which damage is based on the nature of hazards and construction
factors, and where:
•
All fire protection systems are in service and functioning as designed.
•
Full facility Industrial Fire Brigade (Or Plant Emergency Organization) and
Municipal Fire Department response expected.
•
Credit is given to all properly maintained fire barriers up to their design duration
rating
•
Construction features function as designed.
Level II
Primary Protection Systems are not functioning, Manual firefighting response only
A level II Loss Event is one which occurs when:
•
The fire protection system protection the area with the largest PD / BI potential
is impaired or is rendered inoperative or ineffective due to the nature of the
event. Adjacent fire protection systems are presumed operational unless
rendered inoperative or ineffective due to structural failure. Same applies for
the use of special extinguishing systems.
•
Credit can be given for adequate manual emergency response
•
Credit given to minimum adequately maintained (including fire doors and fire
penetrations) 3 hour rated walls where the combustible loading is light to
ordinary, structural failure is not expected, and roof assembly is a listed or
approved noncombustible.
•
Combustible roof construction (including combustible or unknown metal deck
assemblies) results in a contiguous structure loss.
Damage may be limited to the area where the impaired protection system is
located and the nearby surroundings or may extend to the nearest adequate
separation or properly designed and approved construction cutoffs, depending on
site conditions.
Level III Fire Protection Systems are not functioning and no manual firefighting response
A level III Loss Event is one which occurs when:
•
All fire protection systems throughout the entire site or facility are impaired.
•
No credit is given for manual emergency response.
•
Damage is limited only by adequate separation and/or free-standing 4-hours
rated firewalls or equivalent. (Equivalencies must be well defined and proven.)
•
Combustible roof construction (including combustible or unknown metal deck
assemblies) results in a contiguous structure loss.
The size of this loss can approach the value of the buildings of origin or an entire
facility, depending on site layout.

sections.title: Construction
sections.text:
[Site Map]
Source: One Map
Construction Narrative
[PROPERTY] is a 46-storey building with 3 basement levels. The building is of fire-resistive
construction with reinforced concrete load-bearing columns/beams, reinforced concrete floor
slabs and a concrete flat roof. Internal walls are of masonry construction except for the
reinforced concrete core structure. Partition walls within the office spaces comprise of drywall
constructed from gypsum boards, aluminium stiffeners and rock wool insulation in between.
The building has a unitized aluminium glass curtain wall facade with double glazed low E-solar
tinted or single thermal toughened glass. Aluminium spandrel panels have been fitted between
the glass curtain wall panels (level with the building floor plates) and these are bonded with
50mm thick rock wool insulation. The gaps between the curtain wall/spandrel system and
concrete floor slabs are filled with 135mm thick rock wool (2 hours fire rated). There is no
combustible insulation utilized on the facade of [PROPERTY].
[PROPERTY] has a total gross floor area (excluding car park areas but including car park
auxiliary areas) of [AREA]m2. The [PROPERTY] car park occupies the 3 basement levels and
has a total of 351 parking lots in addition to 6 handicap lots. Car parking areas take up a total of
19,567m2, with floor area breakdown (across the 3 basement levels) as follows:
•
Basement 1 – [AREA]m2
•
Basement 2 – [AREA]m2
•
Basement 3 – [AREA]m2
[PROPERTY] was awarded the Building Construction Authority (BCA) Green Mark Platinum
Award (re-certified every 3 years) and has the following green building features (among others):
•
Low E-coating glass facade
•
Extensive use of LED lightings with motion sensors and photocell sensors
•
Use of District Cooling System to provide efficient air-conditioning
•
Heat recovery wheel (energy recovery heat exchanger)
•
Lifts with regenerative drive system
•
Greenery provision at L1 and L5
•
High efficiency filters for air handling units (AHUs)

Compartmentalization and Fire Divisions
[PROPERTY] and [PROPERTY] is connected at basement 2 carpark area. There is a 2 hours
rated fire shutter installed at the interconnection area. The connection is not in use, and the
fire shutter is permanently shut.
The building’s office floor plates adopt an open-plan concept with no horizontal fire separation
within floors (with exception of utility rooms/compartments). Electrical equipment rooms
throughout the development are constructed of compartment walls and floors having a fire
resistance of at least 2 hours, with fire doors leading into electrical rooms rated to 2 hours.
Cable penetrations were noted to be adequately sealed in all visited electrical equipment
rooms.
There is vertical communication between B3 and B1 of [PROPERTY] via car parking ramps,
and between L1 to L3 via the podium atrium. Electrical and telecommunication riser
compartments within the development are provided with 1-hour fire-rated doors.
Telecommunication risers are triple volume (1=3 storey) compartments and fire-stopped on
every 3 floors. Visited riser compartments were noted to be adequately fire-stopped. There is
a combination of 1 hour and 2 × 1-hour fire doors (via smoke stop/firefighting lift lobbies)
leading into the individual fire stairwell enclosures within the building.
Knock out panels have been provided on the individual office floor plates for the construction
of internal (non-enclosed) staircases within tenant spaces. Currently, there are internal
staircases connecting the following floors: L27 to L29, L34 to L35, L40 to L41 and L45 to L46.
Smoke detector-actuated 2-hour fire-rated roller shutters have been installed around all
internal staircase enclosures at the above locations, serving as vertical fire compartmentation
between floors.
Details on Combustible Construction
Based on site observation and information provided there are no combustible material used for
construction.

Key Features / Processes
Activity / Processes [PROPERTY] is occupied primarily as a multi-tenanted office
building with a retail podium from L1 to L3, in addition to 3
basement levels of car parking.
Employees / Shifts
[PROPERTY] is managed by a property management team from
[CLIENT]. The [CLIENT] team is based in [PROPERTY] and
comprise of the following full-time staff: 1 building manager; 2
building executives; 1 technical manager; 6 technical officers; 12
building supervisors; 2 engineers; 3 concierge staff (shared with
2 other entities); 1 environmental, health and safety (EHS)
manager and 1 customer service manager. A number of these
staff (e.g. EHS manager and customer service manager) have
oversight over both the ORQ and [PROPERTY] developments.
Official [CLIENT] office hours are from 8.30am to 6pm, 5 days a
week. Building supervisors operate 24/7 over 2 shifts with 3
building supervisors’ onsite at any 1 time, while technical
officers operate from 7.30am to 11pm daily over 2 shifts, with 3
duty officers per shift.
Jardine Engineering Company (JEC) has been engaged by
[CLIENT] to be the main building/utility maintenance contractor
for [PROPERTY]. JEC technicians are based onsite. There is a
centralized Building Management System (BMS) monitoring
located at [PROPERTY] T2, B2 loading bay. The centralized
BMS system monitors [PROPERTY] T1 to T3 and ORQ.
JEC manages the properties as a cluster with shared resources.
There are 2 engineers and 2 BMS operators and they support
all properties.
For [PROPERTY] T3, JEC deployed 2 – 3 dedicated technicians
per shift.
Third
parties/tenanted
areas
The occupancy rate is 99%.
The building’s anchor tenant is [TENANT] which occupies 15
floors (L3, L5, L6, L8 to L12, L40 to L46). Other major tenants
include Wong Partnership (occupying 3 floors; L27 to L29) and
Rio Tinto (occupying 1.75 floors; L20 to L21). The retail podium
is occupied by restaurants/cafes on L1 (ground level); an food
court and cafeteria (by [TENANT]) on L2; and the [TENANT]
banking hall and auditorium on L3.
Common Hazards  Common property hazards include fire arising from faults in
electrical equipment/lighting, improperly managed hot work
activities, or commercial cooking operations; and water damage
arising from wet pipe sprinkler actuation or chilled/domestic
water pipe leaks/bursts.
Special Hazards
There is no bulk storage of flammable liquids or gases within the
development. Town gas is supplied to the food court and the
restaurants within the podium. This is piped directly into the
respective tenant units from the gas supplier, City Gas Pte Ltd.
The incoming gas supply arrangements at the individual tenant
units are provided with solenoid safety cut-off valves activated
by gas leakage detectors within the kitchen areas. Solenoid
bypass valves are padlocked (in the closed position) with keys
held by building management to ensure that there is no
unauthorized opening of the bypass valves in the event of a gas
leak. The gas detectors in the respective kitchens are not linked
to the BMS or FCC.
The main incoming gas supply arrangement for the
development is not provided with a solenoid safety cut-off valve.
There are however, gas leakage detectors provided at the gas
supply valve chamber, with alarm(s) monitored at the FCC and
BMS.
Kitchen exhaust ducts extend from the individual tenant kitchens
and combine into a central exhaust duct which terminates on L5
and L7. The responsibility for cleaning of kitchen exhaust hoods
and ducting extending from the F&B kitchens lies with the
respective tenants; this is spelled out in [CLIENT]’s
management regulations. Quarterly cleaning is conducted by
specialist contractor engaged by the tenants. Service reports
verifying the cleaning of kitchen ventilation/ exhaust systems are
obtained by [CLIENT] from the tenants. The development’s
central exhaust ducts (responsibility of [CLIENT]) are cleaned
on an annual basis by a third party contractor.
Storage
Limited to small pockets of back-of house storage belonging to
retail tenants. Engineering equipment/raw materials/spares
storage located in B2 storage rooms control by [CLIENT]. There
are no major warehousing facilities in the development.
Utilities and Infrastructure
Power
Distribution on Site
Underground cables.
Details
2 underground incoming feeders supplied at 22kV. The
incoming power is stepped down before being distributed to
the respective electrical rooms and distribution boards.
Back-up Power
Other than the normal power supply from the grid,
emergency power diesel engine generators are provided to
maintain essential and life safety equipment within the
development.
Back-up power is provided for building essential and
emergency services only by 5 outdoor landlord-owned
diesel generator sets:
-
2 x 1.75MVA at L7
-
1 x 1.5MVA at L39 &
-
2 x 2MVA at building roof
In addition, tenant owned ([TENANT]) generators as follows:
-
5 x 1.5MVA at L7
-
2 x 1.5 MVA at building roof
Transformer Details
There are 13 landlord-owned transformers supplying to [PROPERTY], details as below:
There are other tenant-owned transformers installed in separate rooms on L7 and L39. All
landlord-owned transformer units are indicated to be running (none on standby) with average
utilization rates of less than 50% of their designed capacities. A manual coupling (estimated 2
hours lead time) is required to be performed by the appointed licensed electrical worker (LEW)
for switching of building load between transformer units.

2.5 each

resin dry type

L39 transformer rooms
2.5 each

Transformer rooms (each housing 1 to 2 transformers) are a minimum of 2 hour fire
compartments with 2 hour fire doors, however there are no fire walls separating transformer
units within each room.
Boilers
None installed.
Chillers / Cooling Towers
Chilled water for the building’s central air-conditioning system is supplied via a district cooling
system (DCS) operated by Singapore District Cooling (located at 2 sites: B2 of ORQ and at
the [LOCATION] Sands).
The development’s air-conditioning system comprises of a network of air-handling units
(AHUs) and heat exchangers, supported by a chilled water circulation system driven by a
number of circulation pumps. There are 4 x heat exchangers and 5 x chilled water pumps in
B3. This is in addition to a secondary chilled water circuit with 3 x heat exchangers and 3 x
circulation pumps on L39. The B3 heat exchangers are SDC-owned while the L39 heat
exchangers are landlord-owned. All chilled water pumps are landlord-owned and installed with
at least N+1 redundancy. Each level of [PROPERTY] is served by 2 AHUs with ducted return.
In the event when chilled water supply from DCS is disrupted, there are 5 x 400RT landlord-
owned air-cooled chillers (all on standby) on the building roof which serve as backup chilled
water supply for essential utility rooms, as well as for tenants’ use (by agreement only). These
chillers are backed up by emergency power and can support up to 20% of the buildings’ total
cooling requirements. [TENANT] has also installed it’s own chillers (on L7) for backup chilled
water supply.
Landlord-owned air-conditioning systems (AHUs, pumps, air-cooled chillers, VRV units, etc.)
are serviced and maintained on a monthly basis by JEC.
There are no cooling towers installed.
Fuels and Energy Supplies
Each generator set is installed within a metal enclosure and is supplied with a ~700L diesel
day tank. Day tanks are double-walled with leak detection provided between the inner and
outer walls; these are monitored via the BMS. The day tanks are supplied via 3 x 30,000L
underground storage tanks (USTs) located in B3. Diesel from the USTs is automatically
pumped to the generator day tanks via transfer pumps (in the B2 fuel pump room) when a pre-
set low level is reached.
The generator enclosures are provided with spot-type heat detectors linked to solenoid shut-
off valves on the incoming diesel pipelines; these will cut off diesel supply in the event of a fire
within the enclosure. The 3 USTs are installed within individual 4-hour rated sand-filled
concrete enclosures which are provided with dedicated leakage detection sensors.

sections.title: Fire Protection
sections.text:
Site Fire Protection Abstract
The fire protection water supply system, automatic water-based fire protection systems, fire
detection & alarm systems, and manual fire-fighting means installed within the site are
primarily designed and installed to local code, namely: CP 52:2004 (Code of practice for
automatic fire sprinkler system), CP 10:2005 (Code of practice for the installation and
servicing of electrical fire alarm systems) and SS 546:2009 (Code of practice for emergency
voice communication systems in buildings).  The major components of these systems are UL
listed and/or FM approved.
Engineered smoke control system (ESCS) – Installed in the podium. The ESCS on L1 was
designed by Arup and is a performance-based system, while that on L2 and L3 is designed by
Meinhardt and is a prescriptive-based system (per the local fire code). The ESCS comprises
of a network of smoke curtains, smoke dampers and smoke extraction fans, controlled and
synchronized by an addressable smoke detection system. The podium is segregated into
multiple smoke control zones, with dedicated smoke dampers, extraction fans and detectors
for each zone. Smoke is exhausted via a common duct (which traverses through all zones),
with exhaust vents located on L5 and L7.
The engineered smoke control system is serviced and maintained every month by JEC.
Smoke curtains and exhaust fans are tested at least twice a year.
Automatic Sprinkler Protection
Automatic sprinklers are installed as follows.
Coverage
Entire development with exception of electrical equipment rooms
and riser compartments which are provided with smoke
detectors.
Design standard
CP 52: 2004 (Code of practice for automatic fire sprinkler
system): combination of OH1 (5 mm/min @ 72 m2), OH2 (5
mm/min @ 144 m2) and OH3 (5 mm/min @ 216 m2).
Sprinkler System
Monitoring
The sprinkler system is served by a total of 30 sprinkler control
valves (SCVs) located on various floors of the building; there is 1
SCV for every floor from B3 to L8, and 1 SCV for every 2 floors
from L9 to L48 (roof).
SCVs are strap locked (in the open positions) to mitigate against
inadvertent/malicious tampering and are monitored with tamper
switches.
System Maintenance
The sprinkler systems are preventively maintained by the
appointed fire protection system maintenance contractor. This
includes monthly cut-in/cut-out testing of the fire pumps, in
addition to inspections of system components and indicator
panels. An annual water proving test is carried out at the
individual SCVs as part of fire certificate renewal. Refer to
Appendix for the most recent sprinkler system water-proving test
results.
Special Extinguishing Systems
Wet chemical suppression systems have been installed under the kitchen hoods of F&B
tenants (with commercial cooking operations) throughout the development. Systems are of
different make, with those in visited kitchens noted to be UL 300 listed. Responsibility for
system maintenance lies with the respective tenants; this is spelled out in [CLIENT]’s
management regulations.
A number of building tenants have installed their own total flooding gaseous suppression
systems (e.g. FM 200) to protect their high-asset IT equipment/server rooms. Responsibility
for system maintenance lies with the respective tenants.
Water Supply Details
The sprinkler system for [PROPERTY] is designed in accordance to CP52: 2004 for OH 1 and
3; OH3 system covers the basement and podium levels, while OH1 system covers all other
areas.
The sprinkler system is supplied via a combination of gravity feed and 4 sets of sprinkler booster
pumps, each set comprising of 1 duty pump, 1 standby pump and 1 jockey pump drawing suction
from dedicated fire water tanks. All pumps are driven by electric motors and provided with
backup power supply (via diesel generator sets). Details on the pump systems are provided
below:
Sprinkler coverage from L13 to L26 of [PROPERTY] is gravity-fed from the L39 fire water tank.
The fire water tanks are supplied via the public mains and also supply to the building’s wet riser
(both tanks), transfer pump (B3 tank) and hose reel (L39 tank) systems. There are a set of
transfer pumps (1 duty, 1 standby; both Ajax Elite MT100/3 – A20C pumps with rating of 12.5L/2
@ 215m head) in the B3 fire pump room which supply water from the B3 tank to the L39 tank.

Manual Fire Fighting Features
Distance to Fire Department < 1.5 km to [LOCATION] Fire Station
Fire Department Type
Public fire brigades by Singapore Civil Defence Force
(SCDF)
Response Time (minutes)
< 10 minutes
Hydrant Coverage
There are 3 private yard hydrants strategically provided
connected directly to public water.
Fire Hydrant Type
Below ground, private, with double pillar outlets.
Industrial Fire Brigade
NA
Portable Extinguishers
Portable fire extinguishers have been provided at strategic
locations throughout the development. These comprise of
ABC dry powder type extinguishers of various sizes.
Fire extinguishers within building common areas are
inspected on a monthly basis by in-house technicians and
serviced/maintained on an annual basis by contractor.
Extinguishers were noted to be adequately tagged with their
service records and clearly marked with signage.
Hose Stations / Reels
Full coverage per local codes.
Internal 25mm diameter, 30m length hose reels have been
provided at strategic locations throughout the common areas
of the development. There are 5 hose reel stacks extending
throughout all floors of the tower. The hose reel system is
supplied via a combination of gravity feed and a total of 2
sets of hose reel booster pumps, each set comprising of 1
duty and 1 standby electric motor-driven pumps. The pump
sets are installed in the B3 fire pump room (serving B3 to L9)
and on the building roof (serving L38 to L48), with system
coverage for all other floors being gravity-fed from the L39
and roof fire water tanks.
Hose reels systems are serviced and tested on an annual
basis, with visual inspections of individual hose reels carried
out on a half-yearly basis.
Risers (Dry / Wet)
[PROPERTY] is protected by a wet riser system, with 2 wet
riser stacks extending throughout all floors of the tower, and
an additional 5 stacks covering the podium section. The
system is supplied via a combination of gravity feed and 2
sets of wet riser booster pumps, each set comprising of 1
duty, 1 standby and 1 jockey electric motor-driven pumps
drawing suction from dedicated fire water tanks.
Other Manual Firefighting Appurtenances / Comments:
3 street hydrants strategically provided connected directly to public water. Public street
hydrants are drawing water directly from the municipal water supply which is considered as
very reliable in Singapore.
Fire Alarm Monitoring
Automatic fire detection in the form of spot-type smoke detectors is provided within electrical
equipment rooms (transformer rooms, electrical switch rooms, MDF rooms, etc.) and
electrical/ telecommunication riser compartments throughout the building. Smoke detectors
have also been installed throughout the 3 storeys of podium. Heat detectors have been
installed within the individual outdoor generator set enclosures.
Manual break glass call points with fire alarm bells are installed at strategic locations
throughout the development.
The fire alarm system and fire detectors are serviced and tested by Siemens monthly.
Alarm Signaling
Services
The main fire alarm panel is located within the FCC on L1 which is manned 24/7.
The fire alarm signal is monitored by appointed third party vendor, Chubb, known as
providing Decentralised Fire Alarm Monitoring (DECAM) services. Usually within a
timeframe of two minutes or shorter, the local fire brigade will be notified via DECAM
services if there is no response by the local site on any fire alarm signal received.

sections.title: Security
sections.text:
Site Perimeter
Vehicle Access
Vehicles hourly and season parking are allowed in this site.
Typical entry gantry with CCTV monitoring provided.
Perimeter Fencing
Not provided.
Entry Provisions Posted
Security guard station at the building main entrance and other
strategic locations.
No Trespassing Signage
Not provided.
Fencing Height
Not provided
Exterior Lighting
Along the perimeter
Building Physical Features
Ground Level Windows
Secure
Full height glass panel wall on ground level. Entrance to the
buildings are by access control.
Lock and Key Control
Each area is provided with access control via staff / visitor /
contactor, security badge with differentiation in access based
on needs basis.
Office and retail tenants will provide their own access control in
their respective units, which is lock & key or access card
system.
Security Staff / Guards
On-Site Guards
24/7 security for the development is provided by contract
guards from a third party security agency, Prosegur. Guards
are unarmed and perform 12 hour shifts, with 7 guards
during the day shift and 6 guards in the night shift. Guards
are deployed at the security counters, access points and
common areas of the development.
Visiting Patrols
All security personnel have gone through proper training
stipulated by the local regulatory authority.
Police Surveillance
Regular patrol is expected to be conducted by the local
police in the vicinity.
Recorded Rounds
Regular security patrols are carried out for the entire
development including the building perimeters, common
Security Staff / Guards
areas, roofs and M&E plant rooms. An electronic clocking
system is utilised during patrols, with a total of 193 installed
clocking points.
Rounds Frequency
Day: 4 physical clocking
Night: 4 physical clocking
CCTV
Around 500 CCTV cameras have been installed throughout
the development. These cover both internal and external
areas including the main building lobbies, car parks, building
perimeters, lift lobbies and interiors of lift carriages. CCTV
footage is recorded via a DVR system at the FCC, with
storage capacity allowing for at least 30 days of footage to
be stored/played back. CCTV cameras covering critical
areas (e.g. entrance points) are equipped with video
analytics capabilities.
Intruder Detection
Motion Sensors
CCTV cameras are equipped with Video Content Analysis
(VCA), allowing constant monitoring of certain areas for
intrusion, slip & fall, illegal parking, etc.

Yes

Yes, by CCTV.

Yes, all contractors are required to change passes before
commencement of work. Visitors are only given access after

Other Security Programs / Controls
Emergency Response
Documented emergency response plan has been
established. Company Emergency Response Team (CERT)
is available during operational hours. Each CERT team has 5
first responders. All CERT members had undergone relevant
training according to their appointed roles. Some of the
training include industrial firefighting/rescue and first aid
training by SCDF-certified third party training provider.
Drills and table top exercises are conducted 2 x per year

process.
Safe / Vaults

Mobile Equipment Storage

Cash / Check Management

reference:
The [PROPERTY] ([PROPERTY]) is a mixed-use development that occupies a [AREA]
waterfront site at the heart of Singapore’s New Downtown. The entire development comprises
of 3 office towers ([PROPERTY]s 1, 2 and 3), 2 residential towers ([LOCATION] Residences
and [LOCATION] Suites) and a retail mall ([LOCATION] Link Mall). [PROPERTY] was
constructed in 2 phases, with its first phase completed in 3Q 2010 and its second phase in
2012.
The first phase consists of [PROPERTY]s 1 and 2, [LOCATION] Residences and [AREA]m2 of
the retail mall. The second phase comprises [PROPERTY], having 7,850m2 of the retail mall
and [LOCATION] Suites. The scope of this report is limited to [PROPERTY]s 3, a 46 storey
office building with 3 basement levels. [PROPERTY] is jointly owned by [PROPERTY
OWNERS] through an investment holding company, [PROPERTY] LLP. [CLIENT] is the asset
and facilities manager for [PROPERTY] [PROPERTY].
[PROPERTY] is a 99-year leasehold property (commencing from [DATE]) which obtained its
TOP in [DATE]. It is of fire-resistive construction with reinforced concrete load-bearing
columns/beams, reinforced concrete floor slabs and a concrete flat roof. Internal walls are of
masonry construction except for the reinforced concrete core structure. The building features a
3 storey retail podium at its base which houses a number of restaurants, a food court, in
addition to a banking hall.
Sprinkler protection is provided throughout all buildings within the [PROPERTY] development
with exception of the electrical equipment rooms and riser compartments (provided with spot-
type smoke detectors). The sprinkler system is designed in accordance to CP52: 2004 (Code
of practice for automatic sprinkler system). Automatic fire detection in the form of spot-type
smoke detectors is provided within all electrical equipment rooms and electrical /
telecommunication riser compartments throughout the building. Smoke detectors have also
been installed throughout the 3 storeys of the retail podium, while heat detectors have been
installed within individual outdoor generator set enclosures.
Additional fire protection equipment comprise of an engineered smoke control system in the
podium, in addition wet risers, internal hose reels, portable fire extinguishers and manual
break glass call points installed at strategic locations throughout the development. The
buildings are equipped with a fire alarm system which is monitored 24/7 both locally and
centrally via a DECAM station, Chubb.
The [PROPERTY] development is overseen by a property management team from [CLIENT].
The management team has established a high standard of loss prevention programmes for
the site: 24/7 onsite security provided via contract guards; documented emergency response
plan and trained emergency response team; formal permit-to-work system and hot work permit
programme; good housekeeping practices; and a comprehensive preventive maintenance
program for mechanical, electrical and fire protection equipment, among others.
Natural catastrophe exposures for the site are generally low, with exception of flood (moderate
exposure) and lightning (moderate to high exposure).
Changes since Previous Survey
1. Added 3 nos of EV charging lots at B1.
2. Upgraded the building fire alarm system, software and some hardware upgrade.
3. Upgraded the building CCTVs to fully digital with video analytic capability.
Planned Changes / Projects
Ongoing AHU chilled water control valves replacement to smart energy control valves. Project
expected to be completed by end 2026.
